messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: errata in the 2009 book??
parts:
On 12/20/2012 7:18 AM, WGray wrote:
> Hiya,
>
> I am trying to work thru the examples in the book between now and xmas. I
> am getting some simple output differences and am wondering if there is a
> list of errata or changes due to upgrades in R or ggplot2 since 2009. (I
> have searched the web for "errata in Wickham ggplot2 book" and other
> queries but haven't found anything).

I don't know of any comprehensive archive of differences. Most
differences are due to ggplot2 changing. A good way to do this would be
to create a vignette that has all the example code from the book (if
that is even possible given copyright considerations) and then anything
that errors on execution can have its code updated. However, no one has
determined if this is (legally) possible and devoted the time to
creating it.

> Specifically, there are two places where I am getting differences between
> the book and R - p44 and p 45.
>
> p.44 bottom: I type in
> p <- ggplot(msleep, aes(sleep_rem / sleep_total, awake))
>
> then
>> summary(p)
> data: name, genus, vore, order, conservation, sleep_total, sleep_rem,
> sleep_cycle, awake, brainwt, bodywt [83x11]
> mapping: x = sleep_rem/sleep_total, y = awake
> faceting: facet_null()
>
> BUT the book shows:
>
>> summary(p)
> data: <<okay -- same as what R gives me>>
> mapping: <<okay -- same as what R gives me>>
> scales: x, y **** NOT OKAY - R does NOT give me this ***
> faceting: facet_grid(. ~ ., FALSE) **** NOT OKAY - R gives me "faceting:
> facet_null()"

The summary output has changed over time, so this difference is expected.

> I also get differences in the output from summary on the last example on
> this page.
>
> p45
>
> Example in the middle - immediately above the section 4.4 Data -- I type in
> the following:
>
> bestfit <- geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F, color = alpha("steelblue",
> 0.5), size = 2)
>
> BUT R complains to me:
>
> Error in do.call("layer", list(mapping = mapping, data = data, stat = stat,
> :
> could not find function "alpha"
>
> (I even changed my spelling of "color" to "colour" and still R complains.

The alpha function moved from the ggplot2 package to the scales package.
Include

library("scales")

and the code should work.

> Thanks.

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

On Thu, Dec 20, 2012 at 7:18 AM, WGray <gr...@rpi.edu> wrote:

Hiya,

I am trying to work thru the examples in the book between now and xmas. I am getting some simple output differences and am wondering if there is a list of errata or changes due to upgrades in R or ggplot2 since 2009. (I have searched the web for "errata in Wickham ggplot2 book" and other queries but haven't found anything).

Specifically, there are two places where I am getting differences between the book and R - p44 and p 45.

p.44 bottom: I type in
p <- ggplot(msleep, aes(sleep_rem / sleep_total, awake))

then
> summary(p)
data: name, genus, vore, order, conservation, sleep_total, sleep_rem, sleep_cycle, awake, brainwt, bodywt [83x11]
mapping:  x = sleep_rem/sleep_total, y = awake
faceting: facet_null() 

BUT the book shows:

> summary(p)
data: <<okay -- same as what R gives me>>
mapping: <<okay -- same as what R gives me>>
scales: x, y **** NOT OKAY - R does NOT give me this ***
faceting: facet_grid(. ~ ., FALSE) **** NOT OKAY - R gives me "faceting: facet_null()"

I also get differences in the output from summary on the last example on this page.

p45 

Example in the middle - immediately above the section 4.4 Data -- I type in the following:

bestfit <- geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F, color = alpha("steelblue", 0.5), size = 2)

BUT R complains to me:

Error in do.call("layer", list(mapping = mapping, data = data, stat = stat,  : 
  could not find function "alpha"

(I even changed my spelling of "color" to "colour" and still R complains.

Thanks.

--
